summary: Crash and/or data corruption upon attempting to save a world with a world border center over 30 million blocks
description: The bug Attempting to save a world with a world border center over 30 million blocks causes the player to be unable to respawn. The game crashes (Exception generating new chunk caused by java.lang.ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException), and/or the world is corrupted (java.nio.channels.OverlappingFileLockException: null), and you become unable to open it again. "Negative index in crash report handler (0/15)" is spammed to the debug log. To reproduce 1. Create a new world. 2. Execute /worldborder center 50000000 50000000. 3. Execute /kill. 4. You are unable to respawn. 5. Attempt to go to title screen. 6. The game crashes, or the world becomes unable to be opened again.
Steps to Reproduce:
1. Create a new world.
2. Execute `/worldborder center 50000000 50000000`.
3. Execute `/kill` to kill the player.
4. Attempt to respawn and observe that you are unable to do so.
5. Attempt to go back to the title screen.
6. Observe that the game crashes or becomes unable to open the world again.
Environment: Minecraft Java Edition Versions: 21w39a, 21w40a, 21w41a, 21w42a, 21w43a, 21w44a, 1.18 Pre-release 1 (includes snapshots)
Observed Behavior: When attempting to save a world with a world border center over 30 million blocks, such as at coordinates 50,000,000 50,000,000, the game encounters significant issues. Specifically, after setting the world border and killing the player, you are unable to respawn. Attempting to return to the title screen results in the game crashing or rendering the world corrupted. The crash is accompanied by a java.lang.ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException indicating an issue with chunk generation, and a java.nio.channels.OverlappingFileLockException suggests problems with file handling during save operations. Additionally, "Negative index in crash report handler (0/15)" messages are repeatedly logged in the debug log. This bug can be consistently reproduced by creating a new world, setting the world border center to 50,000,000 50,000,000 using the `/worldborder center` command, killing the player with `/kill`, and then attempting to respawn or exit back to the title screen.
Expected Behavior: When attempting to save a world with a world border center over 30 million blocks, the game should not crash or corrupt the world. The player should be able to respawn normally and navigate back to the title screen without any issues. No exceptions or errors should occur in the debug log, and the world should remain fully accessible and playable.
